{{Short description|Indo-Canadian mathematician (born 1956)}}
[[File:Kumar Murty.jpg|thumb|220px|Kumar Murty]]
'''Vijaya Kumar Murty''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} (born 20 May 1956) is an [[Indo-Canadian]] mathematician working in [[number theory]].

==Biography==
Murty obtained his BSc in 1977 from [[Carleton University]] and his PhD in mathematics in 1982 from [[Harvard University]] under [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]].

He and his brother, [[M. Ram Murty]], have written more than 20 joint papers.<ref>[http://www.ams.org/mathscinet/search/publications.html?pg1=INDI&s1=128555%20and%20128560 List of papers at Mathematical Reviews] [[American Mathematical Society]].</ref> In a book edited by Alex Michalos,<ref>Alex Michalos (editor), The Best Teacher I ever Had, Personal Reports from Highly Productive Scholars, The University of Western Ontario, London, 2003, 290p. {{ISBN|0-920354-53-X}}.</ref> there is a description of how the Murty brothers learned mathematics in their teens.

==Awards==
Murty received the [[Coxeter–James Prize]] in 1991 from the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.math.ca/Prizes/info/cj.html Coxeter-James Prize] [[Coxeter-James Prize]], Canadian Mathematical Society.</ref> He was elected to the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 1995.<ref>[http://www.rsc.ca/submitsearch.php?sFirstName=&sLastName=murty&sAcademy=&sAffiliation=&sElection=&btnSearch=Search] Search page on Royal Society Home Page.</ref> In 1996, he, along with his brother, M. Ram Murty, received the [[Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize]]<ref>[http://ffsb.espais.iec.cat/en/the-ferran-sunyer-i-balaguer-prize/ The Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize] Retrieved 2019-01-02.</ref> for the book "Non-vanishing of L-functions and their applications."<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/la/book/9783034802734|title=Non-vanishing of L-functions|author=M. Ram Murty and V. Kumar Murty|publisher=[[Springer Science & Business Media]]/[[Birkhäuser]]|year=1996|pages=196|isbn=978-3-0348-0273-4}}</ref>

In 2018, the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] listed him in their inaugural class of fellows.<ref>{{citation|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|title=Canadian Mathematical Society Inaugural Class of Fellows|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|date=December 7, 2018|access-date=January 7, 2020|archive-date=January 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122125232/https://www2.cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was named a [[Member of the Order of Canada]] in 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Appointments to the Order of Canada – December 18, 2024 |url=https://www.gg.ca/en/appointments-order-canada-december-2024 |publisher=Governor General of Canada |access-date=May 5, 2025}}</ref>

Murty is a professor at the [[University of Toronto]]. In 2025, he was appointed as the founding director of the [[Lodha Mathematical Sciences Institute]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics will drive India's development: An exclusive interview with Prof. V. Kumar Murty |url=https://indiacsr.in/mathematics-will-drive-indias-development-an-exclusive-interview-with-prof-v-kumar-murty/ |website=India CSR |access-date=17 January 2026}}</ref>
